title: Report RP-74: Syrian rue, acacia bark and ephedrine
source: Retold in full from FreeODwiki report RP-74, with the person’s private details left out and the report’s mistakes pointed out.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: In January 2023 a 19-year-old, known in an online drug-use community for posts on chemistry and pharmacology, died after a single day of preparing and taking several substances. The cause of death was given as multiple organ failure from poisoning.
Early in the morning they boiled Syrian rue seeds, which hold harmala alkaloids, an MAOI. In the early afternoon they swallowed 24 asthma tablets whose ingredients include ephedrine.

That evening, with the ephedrine still working, they broke up about 20 g of acacia bark bought online, by hand, and boiled it with the rue for more than an hour and a half. They drank the brew a little before 8 pm. Within about 25 minutes they were badly confused, with intense and frightening hallucinations.
Knives had been left within reach, and they hurt themselves while delirious. Their father found them. They were resuscitated for a long time but could not be saved.

sections.heading: Why it was so dangerous
paragraphs: An MAOI with ephedrine. Harmala alkaloids stop the body breaking down ephedrine and the noradrenaline it releases. Blood pressure can climb into a hypertensive crisis: bleeding in the brain, burst blood vessels, heart failure. The report names this as the main cause. The small amount of opioid in the tablets was not the main danger.

Acacia bark with an MAOI. Some acacia species hold 5-MeO-DMT as well as DMT, and the bark seldom says which species it is. 5-MeO-DMT with an MAOI is one of the most dangerous combinations there is. Boiling for a long time draws out more of whatever the bark holds.
Unknown plant material. Bark sold online may have been sprayed with pesticides, which the report thinks sped the poisoning.
No sitter, and sharp things left out. A sober person in the room, and knives put away beforehand, might have prevented the injuries.

sections.heading: What the report gets wrong
paragraphs: Notes from months earlier, kept in the same report, claim caffeine is an MAOI and that caffeine with harmala alkaloids is "about the same as MDMA". Both are wrong. Caffeine is not a meaningful MAOI, and an MAOI with stimulants is the very kind of mix that raised blood pressure here. Don't act on those notes.

The report also keeps the person's earlier DXM diary: memory gaps, confusion, not recognising their own home, irritability for days afterwards, and their own conclusion that repeated DXM use was a mistake.

sections.heading: What to take from it
paragraphs: Never mix an MAOI (Syrian rue, ayahuasca, harmala alkaloids, moclobemide and the like) with ephedrine, pseudoephedrine, cold or asthma tablets, amphetamines, MDMA, DXM, SSRIs or 5-MeO-DMT. Let at least a full day pass between them, either way round.
Don't brew plant material when you don't know the species or where it came from.
Have a sober sitter, and put knives and sharp things away before you start.
A pounding headache, chest pain, confusion, a racing heart or a high temperature after a mix like this is an emergency. Call an ambulance and say what was taken.

summary: A 19-year-old died after 24 ephedrine asthma tablets and a home brew of Syrian rue and acacia bark. What happened, why it was deadly, and what to take from it.
